prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Dallas for a truck accident case?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” personal injury lawyer for every truck accident case — the right attorney depends on the facts of your case and what you value (trial experience, size of firm, communication style, budget). I can help you find a great lawyer, but here’s how to identify the best one for your situation and what to do next.

How to choose the right truck-accident lawyer
- Trucking-specific experience: look for lawyers who regularly handle commercial truck cases and understand FMCSA regulations, electronic logging devices (ELDs), driver hours-of-service, and common carrier liability issues.
- Resources and experts: truck cases often require accident reconstructionists, medical experts, vocational experts, and investigators. Make sure the firm has those resources or pays for them.
- Trial experience and results: ask about verdicts and large settlements in truck cases, and whether the lawyer will actually try the case if needed (not just settle).
- Board certification and professional membership: check for board certification in relevant areas (e.g., civil trial law/personal injury where applicable), membership in the American Association for Justice or state trial lawyers associations.
- Communication and team: who will handle day-to-day work — the principal attorney or junior staff? How often will you get updates?
- Fee structure and costs: most truck-injury lawyers work on contingency, but confirm the percent, who pays litigation costs, and what happens if you lose.
- Local knowledge and reputation: experience in Dallas courts and relationships with local experts and judges can help.
- Discipline and standing: confirm license status and disciplinary history at the State Bar of Texas website.

Where to look for good candidates
- Texas State Bar Lawyer Referral & Information Service
- Dallas Bar Association referral programs
- American Association for Justice member directory
- Texas Trial Lawyers Association
- Lawyer review sites (Avvo, Martindale-Hubbell) — read reviews but verify credentials

Questions to ask at your first consultation
- How many truck cases have you handled? How many in Dallas County?
- What were your recent verdicts/settlements in truck cases?
- Will you handle my case or will it be passed to an associate?
- How do you handle case costs? What is your contingency fee?
- How long do you expect this case to take?
- What is your strategy for establishing liability against the trucking company?
- Can you provide client references or case summaries?

Red flags
- Guarantees of a specific outcome or dollar amount
- Refusal to provide fee terms in writing
- No trial experience in serious truck cases
- Poor responsiveness during the initial contact

If you want, I can:
- Provide a tailored shortlist of experienced Dallas truck-accident lawyers (with contact info and why they might fit), or
- Help you prepare for initial consultations (a checklist and script), or
- Review names you already have and offer guidance.

Which would you prefer? If you want a shortlist, tell me any preferences (budget, trial-focused, large firm vs boutique, catastrophic injury or wrongful death) and basic details of the accident (date, severity) if you’re comfortable.
